summary_md: **Steins ([@FooSteins](https://x.com/FooSteins/status/2116540969432785148))** highlights *Trial by Trace* by Cao et al. ([arXiv 2610.32285](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32285), [project](https://tracelite.ai/trial-by-trace.html)), which scores harness behavior separately from task success; across 3,420 runs (4 harnesses x 9 models x 95 tasks) 31.1% passed while breaking a harness rule and only 8.4% were fully clean, with Claude Code 73.5, OpenClaw 71.8, DeepSeek Harness 71.0 and Codex 65.2.

Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution

media.description: TraceTrial-Bench framework: task design across seven reliability dimensions, native-harness evaluation with trajectory tracing, multi-source evidence acquisition and failure attribution.
TraceTrial-Bench overview showing that task outcomes can mislead (31.1% of runs pass agent criteria but fail a harness criterion), model-harness interaction, and evidence-based failure attribution.
Layer-wise agent versus harness criterion scores, outcome composition for Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness and OpenClaw, and candidate-link incidence.

Bar charts of overall scores by model (Opus 5 73.3, Kimi K3 72.0, Gemini 3.7 Flash 71.7, Grok 4.6 71.5 ... HY3 66.9) and by harness (Claude Code 73.5, OpenClaw 71.8, DeepSeek Harness 71.0, Codex 65.2).
Overall score versus mean cost per run (log scale) for model and harness combinations, showing a cost-performance frontier.
